summary: A possible need is assumed; no clear customer hypotheses.
Secondary market research; first problem/need hypothesis.
Primary feedback from a few users or experts; hypothesis updated.
Problem confirmed by multiple customers; segments and buyer roles identified.
Customers confirm the product can solve their problem (problem-solution fit).
Customer testing confirms value; structured sales activities started.
Customer agreements in place; first or test sales; small active user base.
Market-ready product sold near target price; initial traction; sales process staffed.
Widespread, repeatable, scalable sales; significant traction.
Research results with potential applications; vague technology idea.
Technology concept defined; applications speculative.
Lab tests show the concept could work; active R&D started.
Components integrated and working together in the lab (initial validation).
Components validated in a relevant (simulated) environment.
Representative prototype demonstrated in a relevant environment.
Near-complete prototype works in an operational environment.
Complete technology proven in actual operations by first users.
Scalable technology proven in operations by several users over time.
Vague business idea; little market or competition insight.
Business concept and value proposition described; brief market familiarity.
Proposed business model (e.g. canvas), TAM/SAM estimates, competition defined.
Simplified P&L indicates viability; initial sustainability assessment (own assumptions).
Revenue and cost sides validated with external feedback; P&L updated.
Complete sustainable business model tested in realistic scenarios (pilot, pre-order).
First commercial revenue shows willingness to pay; key partner agreements in place.
1-3 years of operations show the sustainable model holds; channels and supply chain live.
Sustainable business model operational and proven profitable and impactful over time.
Hypothesising that results might contain some form of IP.
IP forms mapped; ownership clarified.
Key IP described in detail; initial protectability evaluation.
Protectability confirmed by professional; priorities decided.
Draft IP strategy; first formal application of key IP filed.
Complete IP strategy; positive response from authorities; freedom-to-operate assessed.
Key IP in national/regional phase in relevant markets.
IP strategy fully implemented; key IP granted in first market.
IP strategy proven to create value; key IP granted in several countries.
Individual lacking key competencies.
1-2 people with limited competencies; first idea of needs.
Some competencies present; gaps identified with a near-term plan.
Committed champion; several competencies present; roles being discussed.
Founding team with main competencies; shareholder agreement signed.
Complementary, diverse founding team with clear CEO; advisors being recruited.
Well-functioning team with clear roles; board and advisors operational.
Experienced leadership team; competent board; HR processes in place.
High-performing organisation with continuous development.
Little insight into costs or funding options.
Basic plan with funding options for initial milestones.
Funding secured for initial feasibility work (1-6 months).
Verification plan in place and substantially funded.
Investor pitch tested; 12-month budget; funding strategy decided.
Improved pitch tested; 3-5 year P&L and cash flow.
Discussions with investors around a defined offer; business plan in place.
Term-sheet-level discussions; due-diligence materials ready.
6-12+ months runway secured; full financial monitoring.
